proposals.before: Meng Mingyao retreated again and again, yet in the end he triumphed.
proposals.after: Meng Ming retreated again and again, yet in the end he triumphed.
proposals.reason: The Chinese names only 孟明; Mingyao expands the historical 孟明視 identification not present in this sentence.

proposals.before: The dynasty tottered and may yet stand; the temples darkened and may yet see sacrifice again—only you and your brothers can carry the house of Sima through.
proposals.after: The altars of soil and grain were in peril and may yet be restored to peace; the ancestral temples had been displaced and may yet be continued—only you, enlightened lord, and your brothers can broadly rescue the royal plan.
proposals.reason: The Chinese has 明公兄弟 and 弘濟皇猷; 'house of Sima' is an invented gloss not in the source.

proposals.before: When Yuan of Jin sent Gan Zhuo against Zhou Fu at Shouyang, Sun Hui brought his troops in on Gan's side; Zhou Fu broke and ran.
proposals.after: When the Yuan Emperor sent Gan Zhuo against Zhou Fu at Shouyang, Sun Hui brought his troops in on Gan's side; Zhou Fu broke and ran.
proposals.reason: 元帝 is the Yuan Emperor, not the unspecific 'Yuan of Jin'.

proposals.before: He Rui of Lujiang held the Anfeng magistracy while Sun Hui kept a temporary hold on the district.
proposals.after: He Rui of Lujiang was Grand Administrator of Anfeng, while Sun Hui kept a temporary hold on the commandery borders.
proposals.reason: 太守 is Grand Administrator of a commandery, not a magistracy, and 郡境 is the commandery territory.

proposals.before: His grandfather Xiong Qiao had once served Shi Chong as a household steward, yet remained honest and carried himself like a gentleman.
proposals.after: His grandfather Xiong Qiao had once served Shi Chong as a bondservant, yet remained honest and carried himself like a gentleman.
proposals.reason: 蒼頭 is a menial or bondservant, not a household steward; the idiomatic rendering inflates Qiao's status.

proposals.before: Yuan of Jin took his advice.
proposals.after: The Yuan Emperor accepted it.
proposals.reason: 元帝 is Emperor Yuan (Sima Rui). 'Yuan of Jin' confuses the emperor with the biographical subject Xiong Yuan.

proposals.before: Xiong Yuan impeached Diao Xie and stripped him of his post.
proposals.after: Xiong Yuan impeached Diao Xie and had him dismissed from office.
proposals.reason: 奏免 is a memorial requesting dismissal, not Yuan personally stripping the office.

proposals.before: Duke Huan of Qi gave up meat and wine for seven years after a defeat; today's shame runs deeper still.
proposals.after: The Marquis of Qi gave up meat and wine for seven years after a defeat; today's shame runs deeper still.
proposals.reason: Chinese 齊侯 names only the Marquis of Qi; the personal name Huan is supplied by the English without source characters.

proposals.before: When Gu Yi wrote bluntly, Emperor Wu made him magistrate of Tunliu and opened remonstrance posts so straight words had a door—men could speak their minds without fear.
proposals.after: When Guo Yi wrote bluntly, Emperor Wu made him magistrate of Tunliu and opened remonstrance posts so straight words had a door—men could speak their minds without fear.
proposals.reason: 郭 is Guo, not Gu; the English romanization of 郭翼 is wrong.

proposals.before: Gu Yi submitted a memorial, and Emperor Wu promoted him to magistrate of Tunliu; moreover he set up remonstrance officials in order to accept straight speech and draw forward the future, therefore each man could exhaust himself and words had no hidden reserve.
proposals.after: Guo Yi submitted a memorial, and Emperor Wu promoted him to magistrate of Tunliu; moreover he set up remonstrance officials in order to accept straight speech and draw forward the future, therefore each man could exhaust himself and words had no hidden reserve.
proposals.reason: 郭 is Guo, not Gu; the English romanization of 郭翼 is wrong.

proposals.before: Yao drew Shun from obscurity, Shun from mountain caves; the Duke of Zhou did not bend law for kin, nor Shu Xiang for a brother's son.
proposals.after: Yao drew Shun from obscurity, Shun from mountain caves; the Duke of Zhou did not bend law for kin, nor Shu Xiang for his brothers.
proposals.reason: 孔懷 is the classical term for brothers, not a brother's son.

proposals.before: His younger brother Xiong Jin, less famous but still able, served Wang Dun as chief clerk and died as grand administrator of Poyang.
proposals.after: His younger brother Xiong Jin, less famous but still able, served Wang Dun as recorder and ended as grand administrator of Poyang.
proposals.reason: 主簿 is recorder, not the same office as 長史 (chief clerk) in s0190; 終於 marks the terminal post, not an explicit death.

proposals.before: His father Wang Jun had been palace secretary.
proposals.after: His father Wang Jun had been palace aide to the censor-in-chief.
proposals.reason: 御史中丞 is the vice-censor (palace aide to the censor-in-chief), not the palace secretariat; 'palace secretary' names the wrong office.

proposals.before: Once Marquis Shen of Qi feared his army was growing old before battle was joined; how much more now, after three years in armor with lice in the mail—can we not think deeply!
proposals.after: Once, while the Qi army had not yet reached its term, Marquis Shen feared it was growing old; how much more now, after three years in armor with lice in the mail—can we not think deeply!
proposals.reason: 申侯 is Marquis Shen, distinct from Qi; 齊旅 is the Qi army he feared was aging. The idiomatic rendering makes Shen a Qi marquis and drops the army subject.

proposals.before: When Sima Lun seized the throne, the three princes issued the 《Yihai Precedent》 to rank wartime merit, and later even petty favors hid behind that code.
proposals.after: When Sima Lun seized the throne, the three princes issued the 《Yihai Precedent》 to rank wartime merit, and afterward even small merit awards all continued to use that code.
proposals.reason: 論功雖小亦皆依用 means later merit discussions, even small ones, all used the precedent; the idiom invents hidden petty favors.

proposals.before: This was in itself a law for all cases, not a norm for ordinary categories.
proposals.after: This was itself an expedient one-time law, not a standard for ordinary categories.
proposals.reason: 一切之法 here is a temporary expedient, contrasted with 非常倫之格, not a statute for all ordinary cases.

proposals.before: Men like Ma Long and Meng Guan rose from nothing to great deeds, yet war was not their craft and they seldom lasted.
proposals.after: Men like Ma Long and Meng Guan rose from poverty to great deeds, yet because commanding armies was not what they had practiced, they were rarely able to succeed.
proposals.reason: 鮮能以濟 is failure to succeed in command, not that they seldom lasted.

proposals.before: The Yuan Emperor praised him and pardoned him, appointed him adviser, and he then passed through eminent posts to grand administrator of Danyang, grand master of splendid happiness, and was enfeoffed as count of Jianchang.
proposals.after: The Yuan Emperor praised him and pardoned him, appointed him adviser, and he then passed through eminent posts to governor of Danyang, grand master of splendid happiness, and was enfeoffed as count of Jianchang.
proposals.reason: 丹陽尹 is Yin of Danyang, not a commandery 太守.

proposals.before: When Emperor Jianwen assisted the government, he brought him in as marshal to the army that soothes the ruler.
proposals.after: When Emperor Jianwen assisted the government, he brought him in as marshal of the pacification army.
proposals.reason: 撫軍司馬 is the marshal attached to the General who Comforts/Pacifies the Army, not an army that soothes the ruler.

proposals.before: You serve in the field and I in the chamber, yet we both exist to save the dynasty and the house of Sima.
proposals.after: You serve in the field and I in the chamber, yet we both exist to save the altars of the state and to protect house and country.
proposals.reason: 家國 is house and state; the English invents a named Sima house not present in the Chinese.

proposals.before: Gao Song's letter to Huan Wen and Chen Yun's stand against Xie Jie broke reckless mobilization, revived the Run-Ying argument, echoed Guo Jia's bluntness and Zhu Yu's wit—so Huan Wen dropped a rash Xun You scheme and Xie Jie learned to admire Wang Lang's example.
proposals.after: Gao Song's letter to Huan Wen and Chen Yun's stand against Xie Jie broke reckless mobilization, revived the Run-Ying argument, echoed Guo Jia's bluntness and Zhu Yu's wit—so Huan Wen dropped a rash Xu You scheme and Xie Jie learned to admire Wang Lang's example.
proposals.reason: 許攸 is Xu You, not Xun You (荀攸).

proposals.before: He fled Chengdu under an alias and moved Sima Yue with his pen.
proposals.after: He fled Ying under an alias and moved Yue with his pen.
proposals.reason: 違穎 is leaving Ying, not Chengdu; 越 is Yue, corresponding to Sima Yue in the commentary.

decisions.reason: s0029 names only 孟明; the original 'Meng Mingyao' invents a second syllable not in the sentence. The proposed 'Meng Ming' matches the source and remains natural English.

decisions.after: The altars of soil and grain tottered and may yet stand; the ancestral temples faded and may yet be continued—only you, enlightened lord, and your brothers can broadly rescue the royal plan.
decisions.reason: The original invents 'house of Sima' and omits 明公 and 皇猷. The proposal restores those terms, but 'were in peril and may yet' mixes tenses and 'had been displaced' is an awkward gloss of 替. Keep the original hortatory cadence while rendering 社稷, 宗廟, 明公兄弟, and 弘濟皇猷.

decisions.reason: 元帝 is the Yuan Emperor. 'Yuan of Jin' is an unspecific and potentially misleading gloss; the proposed title is accurate.
